description.en: A test sky for a rocket seen from the front and from behind at once: the spiral that dozens of people in Charente saw on 24 March 2025 between 20:55 and 21:10, the upper stage of the Falcon 9 that had launched NROL-69 two hours earlier, braking out of orbit 1 000 km above northern Europe and venting what was left in its tanks while it spun, seen from Angoulême. Not an observer's account: the spiral as physics makes it. The orbit is Marco Langbroek's estimate; the burn, the vent and the spin are assumed; the Sun lighting the exhaust above a dark ground, the flight of every puff and the light are computed.
description.fr: Un ciel d'essai pour une fusée vue à la fois de face et de dos : la spirale que des dizaines de Charentais ont vue le 24 mars 2025 entre 20 h 55 et 21 h 10, le deuxième étage du Falcon 9 qui avait lancé NROL-69 deux heures plus tôt, freinant pour quitter son orbite à 1 000 km au-dessus du nord de l'Europe et vidant ce qui restait dans ses réservoirs en tournant sur lui-même, vu d'Angoulême. Ce n'est pas le compte rendu d'un observateur : c'est la spirale telle que la physique la fait. L'orbite est l'estimation de Marco Langbroek ; le freinage, la vidange et la rotation sont supposés ; le Soleil qui éclaire l'échappement au-dessus d'un sol dans la nuit, le vol de chaque bouffée et la lumière sont calculés.
description.es: Un cielo de prueba para un cohete visto a la vez de frente y de espaldas: la espiral que decenas de personas vieron en Charente el 24 de marzo de 2025 entre las 20:55 y las 21:10, la segunda etapa del Falcon 9 que había lanzado NROL-69 dos horas antes, frenando para salir de su órbita a 1 000 km sobre el norte de Europa y vaciando lo que quedaba en sus depósitos mientras giraba, vista desde Angulema. No es el relato de un observador: es la espiral tal como la hace la física. La órbita es la estimación de Marco Langbroek; el frenado, el vaciado y el giro se suponen; el Sol que ilumina el escape sobre un suelo a oscuras, el vuelo de cada bocanada y la luz se calculan.
description.it: Un cielo di prova per un razzo visto insieme di fronte e da dietro: la spirale che decine di persone videro in Charente il 24 marzo 2025 tra le 20:55 e le 21:10, il secondo stadio del Falcon 9 che aveva lanciato NROL-69 due ore prima, in frenata per lasciare l'orbita a 1 000 km sopra il nord Europa e mentre svuotava ciò che restava nei serbatoi ruotando su se stesso, visto da Angoulême. Non è il resoconto di un osservatore: è la spirale come la fa la fisica. L'orbita è la stima di Marco Langbroek; la frenata, lo svuotamento e la rotazione sono supposti; il Sole che illumina lo scarico sopra un suolo al buio, il volo di ogni sbuffo e la luce sono calcolati.

fromT.rationale: No time is published for the deorbit burn: McDowell puts it over northern Europe at about 20:00 UTC and Nick James saw the cloud rising above Chelmsford's northern horizon at 19:53:15 UTC. Taken as a few seconds of the throttled Merlin Vacuum, the stage turned round so that its exhaust leaves ahead of it, enough to take 0.25 km/s off its speed.

massKgPerS.rationale: The Merlin Vacuum throttled to 60 percent of its 273 kg/s: a short braking burn of a nearly empty stage. Assumed.

fromT.rationale: Eric Barbotin (Charente Libre): after the burn the tanks are emptied, and the propellant freezes and shines as it whirls. The photographs (Charente Libre, Reporterre, L'Actuaire d'Isbergues) show two arms, an S that the Wirral saw first as an hourglass: two opposite vents across the stage's motion. Their speed (0.7 km/s), flow (5 kg/s each for six minutes, the arms reaching the stage in the photographs taken from Charente while the cloud was seen), the share of it that freezes (a tenth, the rest boiling off as gas), how fast each puff spreads (0.15 km/s, a jet opening some twelve degrees into vacuum, so that the arms stay apart for a turn and a quarter and melt into a halo beyond) and the stage's spin (a turn in a minute and a half) are assumed, chosen so that the spiral has the turn and a quarter of distinct arms the photographs show.
